entries.title: Basic Urogenital Anatomy

testable_competencies.anatomy: Use basic genitourinary anatomy to localize common presentations.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational anatomy is assessed within presentation units, not independently.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective supports initial LUTS assessment; this unit supplies the urologic history framework.

testable_competencies.history: Elicit urinary, sexual, constitutional and risk-factor history and identify red flags.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The canonical objective explicitly requires urinalysis interpretation and an initial management plan for hematuria.

testable_competencies.assessment: Differentiate glomerular from nonglomerular hematuria and initiate appropriate evaluation.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly covers adult urinary incontinence and its common stress and urge subtypes.

testable_competencies.assessment: Diagnose common incontinence patterns and initiate initial management.

entries.title: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms and Obstruction

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly requires diagnosis of LUTS causes, severity, predisposing conditions and complications with initial management.

testable_competencies.stabilization: Recognize retention/obstruction, obtain initial investigations, decompress when indicated and escalate complications.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Overactive bladder is a common LUTS cause within the objective's initial diagnostic and management scope.

testable_competencies.assessment: Recognize urgency/frequency syndrome and exclude important alternate causes.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Dysuria, urinary frequency and urgency, and/or pyuria
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly covers the dysuria/pyuria presentations and initial management represented by this unit.

testable_competencies.assessment: Diagnose common urologic infection/inflammation, identify severe or complicated disease and arrange initial management/referral.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No renal-stone objective was found by targeted full-registry search; acute pain offers only an indirect anchor for urgent renal-colic assessment.

testable_competencies.stabilization: Recognize renal colic, investigate for infection/obstruction and arrange urgent escalation when needed.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No renal-mass objective was found by targeted search; hematuria is a genuine but incomplete presenting route to renal-neoplasm recognition.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a renal mass/neoplasm presentation and arrange appropriate investigation and referral.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hematuria evaluation requires recognition of nonglomerular causes; this supports cancer recognition/referral, not oncologic staging.

testable_competencies.recognition: Identify hematuria patterns requiring malignancy evaluation and referral.

entries.title: Prostate Cancer Recognition and PSA Context

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No prostate-cancer objective was found by targeted search; LUTS is an incomplete presentation-level anchor for recognition and referral.

testable_competencies.counselling: Recognize concerning prostate presentations and discuss PSA uncertainty without applying a fixed screening schedule.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly requires distinguishing malignant testicular tumours from other scrotal masses.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize testicular tumour presentation and arrange urgent diagnostic referral.

entries.title: Penile Tumours

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a suspicious penile lesion and refer appropriately.

entries.zero_question_reason: No specific canonical MCC evidence was located; staging and treatment are specialist scope.

entries.title: Acute Scrotal Pain and Scrotal Mass

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Explicit scrotal-mass objective.
Explicitly requires emergent investigation for torsion with sudden scrotal pain.

testable_competencies.stabilization: Treat acute scrotal pain as torsion until excluded and distinguish mass presentations requiring urgent referral.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly requires respectful support and management for sexual dysfunction.

testable_competencies.assessment: Assess erectile dysfunction, contributing disease and medication risk, and provide initial support/referral.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly covers urinary-tract injury diagnosis, severity, complications and initial management.

testable_competencies.stabilization: Recognize renal, bladder and urethral injury; stabilize, investigate and refer urgently.

entries.title: Infertility and Andrology

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Targeted full-registry search located the canonical Infertility objective, supporting couple-level initial assessment and referral.

testable_competencies.assessment: Undertake initial couple-level infertility assessment and arrange appropriate investigation/referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Female-factor assessment overlaps Gynecology; this unit retains the urologic couple-level and male-factor context.

entries.title: Testosterone Deficiency

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize compatible symptoms and refer/coordinate evaluation without fixing testing or treatment thresholds.

entries.zero_question_reason: Targeted full-registry search for testosterone deficiency/hypogonadism found no canonical objective; endocrine treatment thresholds are not frozen.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Targeted search identifies the canonical congenital-anomalies objective; it supports recognition and referral, not detailed corrective procedures.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize common congenital urologic abnormalities and urgent obstructive/infectious complications.

entries.title: Wilms Tumour

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a child with a concerning abdominal/renal mass and refer urgently.

entries.zero_question_reason: No canonical Wilms-tumour objective was located; staging and treatment are specialist scope.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The congenital-anomalies objective is a broad but genuine anchor; it does not name cryptorchidism.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize undescended/ectopic testes and arrange appropriate referral.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective supports diagnosis/initial management of congenital anomalies; this unit limits scope to newborn recognition and multidisciplinary referral.

testable_competencies.stabilization: Recognize atypical genitalia with possible salt-wasting emergency and initiate urgent multidisciplinary assessment.

entries.title: Pediatric Enuresis

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The objective explicitly requires determining whether a medical cause is present in children aged five years or older.

testable_competencies.assessment: Assess enuresis for a medical cause and provide appropriate initial counselling/management.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Source explicitly cross-references Pediatrics; Urology retains bladder-context recognition only.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The enuresis objective is an adjacent pediatric continence anchor but does not specifically name bladder and bowel dysfunction.

testable_competencies.assessment: Recognize bladder/bowel dysfunction and its urinary complication context.

entries.title: Common Urologic Procedures: Catheterization, Circumcision and Vasectomy

testable_competencies.safety: Recognize indications, complications and need for supervision/referral for common procedures.

entries.zero_question_reason: No specific canonical objective located; procedural performance is outside this scope map.

entries.title: Diagnostic and Definitive Urologic Procedures

testable_competencies.context: Recognize procedure names and broad indications only.

entries.zero_question_reason: Endoscopic and definitive-procedure technique/device decisions are specialist scope.

entries.title: Transition-Related Urologic Surgeries

testable_competencies.professionalism: Use respectful language and recognize need for specialist and multidisciplinary care.

entries.zero_question_reason: Detailed reconstructive procedures and protocols are specialist scope.
